task: Make persisted STALE release units resumable only through the canonical fresh reevaluation path, preserving fail-closed semantics and forbidding automatic retry of BLOCKED/FAILED or later lifecycle states.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal replay job 112643423251 used main 9453ef3270fd37ec85d4eb7b38793b713bcc105e and passed trusted Knowledge/Atlas, Plan and Release Risk after the reevaluation dependency repair, but the persisted U01 remained STALE from the prior fail-closed attempt. The top-level driver rejects STALE with RELEASE_UNIT_EXECUTION_STATE_UNSUPPORTED, while core reconciliation currently accepts only PLANNED, so a safely persisted stale unit cannot re-enter canonical reevaluation after its underlying defect is repaired.
observableOutcomes: The driver routes active STALE units to prepareActiveUnit instead of treating STALE as an unsupported terminal state.
prepareActiveUnit always performs fresh semantic successor/unit reevaluation when the active unit is STALE, even if order/base conditions alone would otherwise skip reevaluation.
Core reconciliation accepts STALE only as a source state for fresh reevaluation; successful authorization clears the stale blocker through normal READY transition.
A repeated reevaluation problem returns the unit to STALE with a fresh blocker and does not create a child PR or advance later lifecycle states.
BLOCKED, FAILED, MATERIALIZED, VERIFIED, MERGED and CLOSED are not made automatically retryable by this repair.
unresolvedRisks: Allowing STALE too broadly could accidentally bypass a previous semantic drift decision.
Skipping fresh reevaluation for a STALE first unit whose base happens to equal current main could reuse stale obligations.
A driver-only change would still fail inside reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit because that function currently rejects STALE.
A retry path must not directly mutate persisted blocker/state outside the existing event/CAS authority.

in: Route STALE through the existing prepareActiveUnit path in both drive and single-step executor surfaces.
Force reevaluateSuccessorManifest for STALE in prepareActiveUnit.
Allow reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit to accept PLANNED or STALE as fresh-reevaluation source states.
Add regression proof that STALE retries reevaluate and that non-retryable states remain rejected.
out: No direct release-state edit, blocker deletion, or synthetic transition.
No automatic retry for BLOCKED, FAILED or post-materialization states.
No manual child PR, receipt, merge, or closure fabrication.
No change to decomposition, Release Risk, Atlas authority, storefront, database, auth, payments, inventory, Builder, templates or deployment.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This changes recovery semantics in the trusted release execution state machine. The repair must add exactly one resumability edge while preserving all existing authorization, evidence and fail-closed boundaries.

acceptanceCriteria: Persisted STALE U01 is routed into fresh reevaluation by the canonical driver without manual state mutation.
A STALE unit always runs fresh reevaluation before AUTHORIZE.
reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit accepts STALE only alongside PLANNED and preserves all manifest/base/predecessor/risk/drift checks.
A successful reevaluation transitions through normal AUTHORIZE to READY and clears blocker normally.
A repeated reevaluation BLOCK remains STALE and no PR is created.
BLOCKED and FAILED remain unsupported by automatic driver retry.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle close before merge, then the unchanged rehearsal is replayed from the same persisted CAS state.
invariants: STALE never becomes READY without fresh reevaluation and normal authorization.
No persisted state is edited outside existing state-machine events and CAS persistence.
No automatic retry is added for terminal or policy-blocked states.
Source identity, current-main lease, predecessor receipts, obligation drift and Release Risk authority remain enforced.
Existing exact child proof and PR/merge identity checks remain unchanged.

failureModes: Driver rejects persisted STALE before reevaluation.
Driver routes STALE but core reconciliation still rejects the state.
STALE first unit skips semantic reevaluation because base/order conditions appear fresh.
Repeated semantic drift is accidentally cleared instead of remaining STALE.
Retry support accidentally expands to BLOCKED/FAILED states.
edgeCases: STALE order-1 unit with targetBaseSha equal to current main.
STALE caused by transient reevaluation environment failure now repaired.
STALE caused by real obligation drift that still exists.
BLOCKED or FAILED active unit presented to driver.

alternatives.summary: Treat STALE as a retryable pre-authorization state only by forcing the existing fresh reevaluation and authorization path.
alternatives.reason: Restores resumability without inventing a second state authority or weakening checks.

alternatives.summary: Edit persisted state or clear blocker and change STALE back to PLANNED.
alternatives.reason: Would fabricate authoritative state and invalidate the rehearsal.

alternatives.summary: Route STALE to prepareActiveUnit without changing core reconciliation semantics.
alternatives.reason: Core reconcile currently rejects any state other than PLANNED, so this does not close the execution chain.

alternatives.summary: Automatically retry any state that is not CLOSED.
alternatives.reason: Would weaken policy blocks and lifecycle integrity far beyond the observed missing edge.

specialistReviews.finding: STALE is a recoverable pre-authorization state but there is no canonical transition back through reevaluation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add one explicit STALE -> fresh reevaluation -> AUTHORIZE path across driver, preparation and core reconciliation.

specialistReviews.finding: Simply accepting STALE as READY-capable would let a prior semantic blocker disappear without revalidation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Force reevaluateSuccessorManifest whenever active.state is STALE and retain all existing reconciliation checks before READY.

specialistReviews.finding: The executor must resume from persisted CAS state after a repair rather than requiring state reconstruction.
specialistReviews.resolution: Route STALE through canonical prepare/persist logic and leave all later PR/proof/merge paths unchanged.

specialistReviews.finding: Live rehearsal proved that fail-closed persistence works but recovery from that persisted STALE state is absent.
specialistReviews.resolution: Lock the retry boundary and non-retryable states with regression tests, then replay the same state after merge.

challenge.scenario: U01 is STALE from a previous environment failure, current main and source are now healthy, and the executor is rerun.
challenge.finding: If the driver recognizes only PLANNED and PR_OPEN, recovery stops before reevaluation even though the underlying defect is fixed.
challenge.resolution: Route STALE into prepareActiveUnit in both drive and single-step surfaces, then persist only the resulting canonical state transition.

challenge.scenario: A STALE order-1 unit already has targetBaseSha equal to current main.
challenge.finding: If prepareActiveUnit reevaluates only for successors or base drift, the stale semantic blocker could be bypassed and the old manifest authorized unchanged.
challenge.resolution: Make active.state==='STALE' an independent mandatory reevaluation condition before AUTHORIZE.

challenge.scenario: The driver routes STALE correctly but reconcileSuccessorReleaseUnit still requires execution.state==='PLANNED'.
challenge.finding: Recovery fails one layer deeper with RELEASE_UNIT_RECONCILIATION_STATE_INVALID, leaving the missing edge unresolved.
challenge.resolution: Allow exactly PLANNED or STALE as reconciliation source states; all other states still throw.

challenge.scenario: A real obligation drift remains after retry.
challenge.finding: A recovery feature must not convert genuine semantic drift into READY merely because the previous state was STALE.
challenge.resolution: Run the unchanged obligationDrift/base/risk/predecessor checks; non-PASS result is persisted as a fresh STALE/BLOCKED decision.

challenge.scenario: An active unit is BLOCKED because of forbidden scope or FAILED because of execution failure.
challenge.finding: Treating all blocked-looking states as resumable would weaken release policy and failure semantics.
challenge.resolution: Driver retry branch and reconciliation source-state allowance name STALE explicitly; BLOCKED/FAILED remain unsupported.

challenge.scenario: STALE retry succeeds and a prior blocker object remains attached.
challenge.finding: Downstream state could appear simultaneously READY and blocked if recovery mutates only state flags.
challenge.resolution: Reuse authorizeReleaseUnit, which replaces the fresh manifest, creates execution authorization, sets READY and clears blocker atomically in the canonical state transition.

challenge.scenario: Two executor attempts retry the same STALE state concurrently.
challenge.finding: Both may compute valid reevaluations but only one may authoritatively advance persisted state.
challenge.resolution: Keep persistRemoteExecutionState expectedStateCommit CAS unchanged so stale writer rejection remains authoritative.

challenge.scenario: The retry reaches materialization and an earlier equivalent U01 branch already exists.
challenge.finding: Recovery must not reintroduce the prior non-fast-forward materialization defect.
challenge.resolution: Leave reconcileExactMaterializedCommit unchanged so exact remote branch reuse remains required after successful STALE reevaluation.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Implement the narrow STALE retry edge across driver, prepareActiveUnit and core reconciliation plus regression tests.
Require exact-head Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Replay, Release Risk, full tests, typecheck, build and Completion Truth PASS.
Commit only canonical lifecycle closure metadata and require final exact-head CI PASS.
Merge the fix, verify fresh main CI, then replay the unchanged rehearsal from persisted CAS state and require canonical U01 progression.

requirements.requirement: Persisted STALE release units must be safely resumable only through fresh canonical reevaluation, while policy-blocked and failed states remain non-retryable.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A STALE release unit may not become READY without fresh reevaluation.
BLOCKED or FAILED release units may not become automatically retryable.

notes: Created from live Failure Intake #1003 after rehearsal replay job 112643423251 proved a persisted STALE recovery gap. This revision is plan-only; no state-machine implementation is authorized until Plan Before Code approves the projected scope.
